statement: A quantity $Q$ decays exponentially so that $Q=Q_{0}e^{-kt}$. Given that $Q$ is $80$ at $t=1$ and $40$ at $t=3$, find $k$ and $Q_{0}$, and determine the time at which $Q=10$.
solution: From the two data points, $80=Q_{0}e^{-k}$ and $40=Q_{0}e^{-3k}$. Dividing, $\frac12=e^{-2k}$, so $k=\frac12\ln2$. Then $Q_{0}=80e^{k}=80\cdot\sqrt{2}=80\sqrt{2}$. For $Q=10$: $10=80\sqrt{2}\,e^{-kt}$, so $e^{-kt}=\frac{10}{80\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{8\sqrt{2}}$, giving $-kt=\ln\frac{1}{8\sqrt{2}}=-\ln(8\sqrt{2})$, hence $t=\frac{\ln(8\sqrt{2})}{k}=\frac{\ln(8\sqrt{2})}{\frac12\ln2}=2\log_{2}(8\sqrt{2})=2(3+\tfrac12)=7$.
hints: Divide the two equations to eliminate Q0 and find k.
